final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses real-world problems of contraceptive use among young people in Kwadaso-Ghana and emerging Ethiopian regions: (1) young people face stigma when accessing contraceptives from traditional sources, suggesting a need for social marketing to bypass this barrier; (2) contraceptive non-use is driven by concerns about side effects and health risks, often based on personal experience or information from friends/family or ignorance, indicating a need for individualized counselling and choice; (3) teenagers have less awareness and are exposed to confusing online contraceptive information with limited capacity to filter and process it, so early training before sexual onset is needed to prevent negative sexual and reproductive outcomes; (4) higher-degree students may experience information fatigue, overload, and contaminated information (disinformation/misinformation), reducing risk perception and fostering nonchalant attitudes, so information managers/regulators should ensure high-value, targeted, updateable information without infringing human rights; and (5) off-campus students (older, married, higher income, more knowledgeable) show better contraceptive attitudes, highlighting demographic predictors that should inform tailored interventions.

final_conclusion: The article addresses the real-world problem of low levels of good knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) regarding contraception among female undergraduate TV College students. It identifies predictors of contraceptive use—such as knowledge, Plateau indigenous (majority population) status, and being sexually active—and highlights disparities in awareness, access, and attitudes, particularly among minority populations. The authors call for improved contraceptive information, education, and communication (IEC/ICE), innovative counseling, school-based interventions for tertiary students, review of sex education policies, awareness campaigns via acceptable media, parent–child communication, and reform of advocacy efforts and young people-friendly sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services and policies to improve contraceptive knowledge, attitudes, and utilization among young people.

38 Abstract
39 Background: Scorpion envenomation is a public health problem that results in a life-threatening medical 
40 emergency in tropical and subtropical regions. Paediatric victims are more at risk to severe envenomation 
41 compared to adults. 
42 Objectives: This study aimed to determine clinical features and outcome of patients hospitalized due to 
43 scorpion stings at the Tesseney Community Hospital. 
44 Methods: A prospective, descriptive cross-sectional study conducted from 1st June 2019 to 31st May 2020 
45 on patients hospitalized due to scorpion stings at the Tesseney Community Hospital.
46 Results: 165 scorpion sting patients were admitted during the study period. Majority were older than 15 
47 years old (61.8%) with an approximately equal male-to-female sex ratio (0.94:1). Scorpion sting cases 
48 largely belonged to urban (57%) compared to rural areas. The black scorpion (38.8%) was the 
49 predominately identified scorpion, but in a proportion of cases the scorpion colour was undetermined 
50 (31.5%). The foot was predominate sting site (64.8%) followed by hand (31.5%). A single sting (91.5%) 
51 was more frequently presented compared to multiple stings (8.5%). Majority (94.8%) of scorpion sting 
52 cases occurred during the summer period with highest scorpion stings counts belonging to September and 
53 October. The main clinical manifestations upon presentation were localized pain (70.3%) and sweating 
54 (56.4%) with more severe symptoms exhibited amongst age groups less than 15 years old. The fatality rate 
55 (4.8%) was largely associated age groups less than 15 years old with (p = 0.006, OR: 2.845; 95% CI: 0.656-
56 12.343). 
57 Conclusion: Our study found children experienced more severe envenoming symptoms with related 
58 mortality compared to adults. This study may be a tool to identify at-risk population groups and build 
59 measures to prevent scorpion stings within the western lowlands of Eritrea. 
60 Keywords: scorpion sting, envenomation, clinical features, Eritrea.

71 Introduction 
72 Scorpion stings are a life-threatening medical emergency with frequent presentations within emergency 
73 department in many areas of the world.(1) Accurate global statistical evidence on scorpion stings are not 
74 readily available, but the literature indicates that all settings are usually affected by this medical threat.(2) 
75 In 2018, WHO reported that the true scorpion sting envenomation burden is not known because many 
76 accidents occur in villages within tropical and subtropical countries where victims likely do not seek 
77 medical attention.(3) It is estimated that 1.23 million scorpion stings occur per year with roughly 3250 
78 deaths per year.(1,2,4–6) Developing countries are often reported with higher scorpion envenomation 
79 accidents and related mortality compared to developed countries due to lower socioeconomic structures and 
80 inadequately equipped health facilities.(2) Pediatric victims are more at risk to severe envenomation with 
81 related mortality compared to adults due to their small body size.(4,7) 
82
83
84 Figure 1. Yellow-colored scorpion brought into the ED by family members. Envenomated patient 
85 suffered from irreversible shock and pulmonary edema and was thereafter deceased.
86 Scorpions are predatory arachnids with four pairs of legs, a pair of grasping pedipalps, and a narrow-
87 segmented tail with a characteristic curved back ending with a venomous sting.(5) Scorpions are generally 
88 located in dry and hot environments, although some species also occur in forest and wet savannahs.(5) All 
89 scorpion species are nocturnal, hiding under stones, wood, or tree bark during the day.(5,8) They are coated 
90 in a variety of colours, ranging from straw colour to yellow, and light brown to black.(4) Scorpions have a 
91 remarkable capacity to survive and adapt, allowing them to withstand heat, drought, desert and freezing 
92 conditions which permits the species to survive virtually independently of their environmental 
93 constraints.(5) Currently there are more than 1500 subspecies of scorpion recognized worldwide, with 50 
94 subspecies having dangerous venom for humans.(4,8) The Parabuthus (western and southern Africa), 
95 Hottentotta (south Africa and south-east Asia), Leiurus (northern Africa and middle East), and Androctonus 
96 (northern Africa and southeast Asia) scorpion species are reported to be found within the African 
 . CC-BY 4.0 International licenseIt is made available under a 
 is the author/funder, who has granted medRxiv a license to display the preprint in perpetuity. (which was not certified by peer review)
The copyright holder for this preprint this version posted January 2, 2024. ; https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.01.02.24300701doi: medRxiv preprint 
97 continent.(5) Within East Africa, scorpion sting cases are common in the central-west regions of Sudan due 
98 to geographical location, climate, and the socioeconomic structure.(8,9) Though there is no ecological 
99 survey of scorpion species done within Eritrea, scorpion sting accidents are found to be common in the 
100 western lowlands of Eritrea which borders Sudan.
101 Scorpion venom is a “cocktail” of complex structures formed by neurotoxic proteins, acidic proteins, salts, 
102 and organic compounds, with variable compositions and lethality amongst subspecies.(4,5,8) Venom 
103 mainly effects neurologic, cardiovascular, respiratory, hematologic, and renal systems with local effects 
104 around the sting site (i.e. redness, pain, swelling, and burning).(4,8) Toxins and enzymes within venom 
105 possess neurological tropism effects that act mainly on voltage-gated sodium and potassium ion channels 
106 on excitable cells of nerves and muscles.(5) Venom from the same scorpion can have multiple toxins that 
107 can interact with each other, modulating the response of the ion channels involved and leading to complex, 
108 rapidly progressive symptoms.(5–8,10–12) The main effect of the venom in a victim is to mediate ion 
109 channels for intense, persistent depolarization of autonomic nerves, leading to massive discharges of 
110 neurotransmitters from both autonomic nervous system branches.(5) This is referred to as an “autonomic 
111 storm” owing to the sudden pouring of endogenous catecholamine into the circulation.(5,11–14) The effects 
112 of an “autonomic storm” are seen throughout the body, but are more serious on the cardiovascular and 
113 respiratory systems leading to arrhythmia, hypertension or hypotension, and pulmonary edema.(15) 
114 Clinically, the “autonomic storm” evoked due to scorpion envenoming is characterized by transient 
115 parasympathetic (vomiting, profuse sweating, ropy salivation, bradycardia, ventricular premature 
116 contraction, priapism in male, and hypotension) and prolonged sympathetic (cold extremities, hypertension, 
117 tachycardia, pulmonary edema, and shock) stimulation.(5,16–19) 
118 Signs and symptoms of scorpion stings are divided into three classes commonly known as the Abroug’s 
119 classification. (4–6,8,11,14,20) Majority of scorpion sting cases only require supportive therapy, including 
120 ibuprofen, cleaning of the sting area, and tetanus prophylaxis. In certain areas of the world where scorpions 
121 are more poisonous (i.e., the Middle East), scorpion stings are treated with drugs and methods that reduce 
122 symptoms and complications.(21) Over the course of the 20 th century, scorpion antivenom (SAV), 
123 vasodilators, and intensive care facilities have significantly reduced the fatality rate of severe scorpion 
124 envenomation.(5) Administering SAV can neutralize unbound circulating venom to reduce the probability 
125 of sympathetic nervous system over-stimulation.(5) Though the benefits of SAV has been proven in some 
126 studies, the effectiveness of SAV continues to be debated.(4,5,19,22) A critical component of scorpion sting 
127 pathogenesis is alpha-receptor stimulation.(5,14) Prazosin is an α1-blocker commonly known as a 
128 pharmacological and physiological antidote to the venom action. The drug acts to relieve serious breathing 
129 difficulty due to high blood pressure.(5,12) As a phosphodiesterase inhibitor, the drug reduces blood 
130 pressure via reducing preload and left ventricular impedance without increasing heart rate.(5) Previous 
131 studies have recommend prazosin as a first-line treatment for patient arriving to the ED with scorpion 
132 envenoming due to the drugs high availability in rural settings.(12,23) 
133 This study aims to describe the clinical manifestations and outcomes of scorpion sting patient cases 
134 admitted at Tesseney Community Hospital. The study seeks to inform medical professionals and public 
135 health workers to design better preventive measures to reduce scorpion sting incidents within Eritrea.

141 Materials and Methods
142 Study design: This was a prospective, descriptive cross-sectional study conducted from 1 st June 2019 to 
143 31st May 2020 for patients admitted to due to scorpion stings at the Tesseney Community Hospital. 
144 Study area: Tesseney hospital is a community hospital located in Gash-Barka region of Eritrea that serves 
145 a catchment population of 87,992 distributed in an area of 1,096.83 km 2 (Figure 2). The hospital provides 
146 inpatient and outpatient services, delivery service, laboratory services, imaging unit, physiotherapy unit, 
147 and possess a 115-bed capacity.

152 Study population: All patients admitted to the hospital due to scorpion stings from 1 st June 2019 to 31 st 
153 May 2020 were considered the study population. 
154 Inclusion and exclusion criteria: Patient who had a history of scorpion sting and had seen or killed the 
155 scorpion (via the victim or bystander) were also included as the study. Patients with a history of unknown 
156 bites, arrived to the ED without signs of life, and/or deceased after discharge from the hospital were 
157 excluded from the study.

158 Data collection and analysis: Data was collected by admitting doctors in a predesigned questionnaire 
159 survey prepared in open data kit (ODK) and were followed until the final outcome. Demographic 
160 characteristics, vital signs, symptoms and signs, time interval between scorpion sting incident and arrival 
161 at the hospital, and medications administered were recorded. Statistical analyses were performed via 
162 Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) v.23 software. The symptoms and signs were categorized 
163 into three classes according to Abroug’s classification (Table 1). The Abroug’s classification was utilized 
164 due to the catalogue’s convenience and its common use in neighbouring countries (Table 1).(4–
165 6,8,11,14,20)  Descriptive data were expressed as frequency and percentage while intergroup differences 
166 were analysed using Chi-Square or Fisher test depending on the characteristics of the data (p-value < 0.05 
167 as statistically significant).

170 Ethical approval: The study received ethical approval from the Ministry of Health Research and Ethics 
171 Approval Committee. A written informed consent was obtained from each patient or parent/care taker for 
172 children. Confidentiality of study participants was maintained by analysing anonymised aggregate data and 
173 coding the personal identifiers. Patients were reassured no environmental or occupational harm by 
174 participating within this study. All patient subjects were provided the available standard treatment for their 
175 disease process.

177 Results 
178 A total of 165 patients with scorpion stings were admitted to the Tesseney community hospital from 1 st 
179 June 2019 to 31 st May 2020. Our results had an almost similar sex distribution (male = 48.5%; female = 
180 51.5%) with a male-to-female sex ratio of 0.94:1. The majority of cases were from urban areas (57%) 
181 compared to rural areas. Majority (61.2%) were older than 15 years old while 38.2% of cases were younger 
182 than 15 years old (Table 2). The mean, median, and standard deviation of age according to their sex were 
183 26.03, 17.50 and 19.73 for males and 23.89, 20.00, 16.56 for females, respectively. According to 
184 educational status, 38.2% of cases were illiterate or had no formal education, 34.4% had elementary level 
185 education, and 27.3% had middle or higher levels of education (Table 2). As to occupational frequency, 
186 shepherds (31.5%), farmers (21.2%), and students (26.9%) ranked the highest while the remaining were 
187 registered as other (21.2%).

191 was found in 65.5% of the cases. The black scorpion (38.8%) was the predominantly identified scorpion 
192 followed by yellow/red/white (30.3%) with the rest declared as unknown (31.5%) (Table 3). The site of 
193 sting was mostly located on the foot (64.8%) followed by hand (31.5%). Concerning the time of the scorpion 
194 sting incident, 62.4% of the sting occurred at night-time compared to 37.6% during the daytime. Indoor

226 Discussion 
227
228 Although medical science has advanced in recent decades, scorpion envenomation has largely been ignored 
229 due to unknown prevalence of scorpion stings and a high number of low-income victims.(2) Majority of 
230 scorpion sting accidents occur in villages in tropical or subtropical regions where the victim do not fully 
231 appreciate the seriousness of the medical threat. Thus, victims rely more on traditional healers and remain 
232 unregistered in a healthcare setting.(3) In this aspect, to reduce the incidence of scorpion stings and their 
233 complications, the 4 th International Conference on Snakebites and Scorpion Stings in Dakar stressed the 
234 need to develop better recording and reporting systems and optimize the gathering of data on scorpion 
235 injuries.(2) The western lowlands of Eritrea have shown to be a conducive area for scorpions with a recent 
236 surge of scorpion stings cases within the region, inciting the need for this study. This study is a descriptive, 
237 cross-sectional study of scorpionism within the western lowlands of Eritrea with study setting based within 
238 the Tesseney Community Hospital. The Tesseney community hospital is the only hospital that receives 
239 scorpion sting cases within the region, other corresponding hospital have no similar reports. 
240 Our study held roughly an equal male-to-female ratio (0.94:1). This finding is in contrast to other studies 
241 that report higher male-to-female ratio within the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region where 
242 deadly scorpion stings are most common.(2,4,21) Male-to-female ratios differ depending on the study 
243 design and region; some studies report higher male-to-females ratios or vice versa.(2,21) These different 
244 findings can likely be attributed to the differing social and demographics factors rather than climate and 
245 geographical factors. Age groups older than 15 years old were more frequently affected by scorpion stings 
246 (61.8%) compared to age groups less than 15 years old (38.2%). The Gash-Barka region is also commonly 
247 known as the “bread basket of Eritrea” with the majority of the older male population employed in 
248 agriculture or animal herding. Scorpion sting victims older than 15 years old usually performed work 
249 outdoors (e.g., shepherd or farmer) and were more likely to be exposed to a scorpion habitat to be stung. 
250 Our results report most victims were from an urban (57%) compared to a rural setting. The literature often 
251 reports scorpion sting victims typically originate from rural compared to urban areas which contrasts with 
252 our findings. Due to the dependence on subsidence agriculture and low socio-economic structure across the 
253 Gash-Barka region in which people living in urban areas were using firewood for cooking from rural areas 
254 may be attributed to increased number. Beside the criteria classifying rural and urban areas is not definitive. 
255 Thus, accurate classification of patient’s place of residence was not possible during the study. 
256 Previous studies report that sting sites are commonly located on the extremities compared to the head or 
257 trunk.(4,11,12) Our results showed that 96.2% of sting sites were located in the extremities with a majority 
258 of sting sites on the foot (64.8%) compared to the hand (31.5%). Scorpion hiding in shoes left empty 
259 overnight or in pockets of loose clothing or trousers are common cause for being stung on the hand or 
260 foot.(5) Furthermore, wearing sandals instead of close-toed shoes, working in unprotected fields, and 
261 children running barefoot are common occurrence within the Gash Barka region due to the predominate 
262 agriculture lifestyle and low socio-economic structure.(4) Our study reports night-time stings (62.4%) were 
263 more common compared to daytime stings which corresponds with previous studies.(2,8) An explanation 
264 for higher night-time stings may be attributed to residents collecting firewood and storing the firewood 
265 inside their residential compound. Firewood is a typical scorpion habitat within the region. As nocturnal

The copyright holder for this preprint this version posted January 2, 2024. ; https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.01.02.24300701doi: medRxiv preprint 
266 animals, scorpions would leave their habitat at night to hunt and may come in contact with a foot or hand 
267 of person sleeping on the floor or elevated bed. 
268 Previous studies have shown the prevalence of scorpion sting accidents are more common during the 
269 summer season than the winter/autumn season.(2,4) Warm temperature and sunny weather are conditions 
270 that leads to higher number of envenomation accidents.(2) Our results aligned with the majority of literature 
271 findings; the western lowlands of Eritrea had the highest scorpion sting incidence during the summer period 
272 (93%) with September and October being the leading months. The MENA region also report similar 
273 conditions with Morocco having the highest scorpion sting incidence between June and September, Saudia 
274 Araba between May and September, and Iran between April and October.(4) Our findings showed that 
275 black-coloured scorpions (38.3%) were the highest report count followed by yellow/red/white (30.3%), 
276 with the remaining cases reported as undetermined (30.9%). A study in Morocco showed similar results 
277 with the most common scorpion colour being yellow (41.7%) and black (27.6%) with the remaining being 
278 unknown (30.7%).(9) A epidemiological study done in south-eastern Turkey also showed that black and 
279 yellow coloured scorpions were predominately identified within their study.(4) 
280 The clinical features of scorpion sting often depend on the subspecies of scorpion, lethality of venom, 
281 venom amount injected, age and feeding characteristics of the scorpion as well as seasonal conditions.(4,8) 
282 Different species of scorpions have different types of venom which may cause local as well as systemic 
283 effects in the first few hours.(1,4,7,9–11,22,24) Systemic manifestations (cardiovascular toxicity, 
284 respiratory failure, hypertension and hypotension, etc) are observed at various sites throughout the body 
285 and appear within the first 12-24 hours following immediate local effects around the sting site.(4) Within 
286 our study, the most common clinical manifestations were localized pain (70.3%), sweating (56.4%), and 
287 vomiting (33.9%). Class II-III manifestations were mainly observed amongst age groups less than 15 years 
288 old with cardiac rhythm disorder, shock, convulsions, and semi-consciousness being the most common 
289 manifestations. In terms of cardiac rhythm disorder, bradycardia was more commonly observed compared 
290 to tachycardia. Overall, these findings align with previous studies that report the severity of envenomation 
291 was found higher in children compared to adults with related mortality rate.(9,13) Age groups less than 15 
292 years old passing away from class II-III manifestations contributed most to the fatality rate (4.8%), likely 
293 due to cardiac dysfunction or pulmonary edema.(4) Patient less than 15 years old (p = 0.006) and had an no 
294 formal education (p = 0.008) showed a possible predisposing risk factor for the severity of symptom or 
295 death. Within the literature, children are often reported with higher severity of scorpion envenomation 
296 symptoms, likely attributed to their smaller body size.(9) With a smaller body mass, venom could diffuse 
297 and act more rapidly on the autonomic nervous system, thus have a higher likelihood of systemic 
298 involvement in which positions an individual to a higher risk of death. 
299 Our results exhibited an unusually high class III envenoming symptoms (43.6%) compared to similar 
300 studies in the literature.(1,22) This was largely due to the villager’s mindset towards arachnid bites or stings. 
301 Upon a scorpion sting accident, adult victims (greater than 15 years old) would likely stay at home if they 
302 feel mild symptoms, relieving their pain by cleaning the sting site using traditional home remedies. Adult 
303 victims would likely seek medication attention only if symptoms from the scorpion sting felt moderate to 
304 severe. This may take as long as day or two after the incident had occurred. Children scorpion sting victims 
305 (less than 15 years old), however, were immediately admitted to a hospital because pain was intolerable. 
306 For adults, the longer elapsed time increased the probability of developing systemic effects and 
307 experiencing an “autonomic storm”, thus classifying the patient symptoms as class III. If adult patients

308 recognized the severity of the medical threat and were hospitalized early-on, medication management and 
309 monitoring would likely prevent systemic effects. 
310 In terms of medication management, Nifedipine and/or SAV were given in replacement of prazosin for 
311 cases presenting with class III symptoms. Nifedipine is often used to treat high blood pressure and is 
312 considered a 2 nd line treatment with subpar results compared to prazosin. Only 15.2% of cases received 
313 either Nifedipine and/or SAV to relieve class III symptoms. Ampicillin or ceftriaxone were often used as a 
314 prophylaxis for critical patients who appeared septic and already possessed a catheter. Diazepam was only 
315 administered when SAV was not given. Diazepam was used as a sedative for patients experiencing 
316 convulsions, shock, and/or restlessness. Within the literature, in cases where severe pulmonary edema, 
317 neurotoxicity, and circulatory failure are present, oxygen, sublingual nifedipine, digoxin, furosemide, 
318 aminophylline, dopamine, vitamin K, and fresh frozen plasma may be given.(4,12,16) Phenobarbital and 
319 dexamethasone may be administered for 48 hours in cases with convulsions.(4,12,16)  
320 Limitation of the Study
321 Our study is a prospective study with data limited from a single hospital within the Gash-Barka region. 
322 Within this region, victims who suffer scorpion stings may not have registered into a healthcare setting, 
323 thus did not have their experience documented. There were also limitations to accurate data recording 
324 include identification of scorpion colour and definitive rural vs urban criteria when registering patients. 
325 Follow-up after discharging patients also was not performed. Thus, fatalities at home days after discharge 
326 were often heard via word-of-mouth and were not included in the study. During the study period, 
327 medication efficacy was difficult to determine as SAV stocks ran-out and prazosin therapy was also not 
328 available due to budget constraints. 
329 Conclusion 
330 Our results indicate the main clinical features of scorpion stings were localized pain, sweating, and 
331 vomiting. Majority of scorpion envenomation victims were older individuals working in agriculture and 
332 unaware to a typical scorpion habitat while performing daily activities. The unusual high level of class III 
333 symptoms is likely a consequence of the villager mindset toward arachnid stings, thus most cases had 
334 immediate effects around the sting site with mild, rarely fatal, systemic involvement. Although the scorpion 
335 sting burden is higher in adults compared to children, our study found that the severity of scorpion 
336 envenomation is greater in children compared to adults. Envenomation severity was indicated by the high 
337 frequency of class III symptoms found in children, such as cardiac rhythm disorder and convulsions, as 
338 well as related fatality rate. 
339 Recommendation
340 Preventive educational programs targeting at-risk groups are instrumental to prevent scorpion sting 
341 accidents and fatalities in resource-limited areas. Enjehay, a small agriculture-based village in the Gash-
342 Barka region, was recently given a prevention health program due to their alarming high scorpion sting 
343 case count compared to their small population size. The program advised to wear close-toed shoes, use 
344 mosquito nets, and to place firewood outside the residential compound (away from beds and children) as 
345 firewood was a common scorpion habitat. Improved awareness of scorpion sting dangers and increased 
346 care-seeking behaviour to a health centre compared to using traditional healing practices was observed by

347 the Tesseney healthcare staff, encouraging broader use of the preventive program. It is also suggested that 
348 further qualitative and quantitative studies be performed to investigate the awareness of scorpion stings 
349 dangers amongst at-risk population groups (i.e., adolescent and children) as well as typical activities that 
350 incite a scorpion sting accident. Investigating healthcare workers care of envenomed patients and capacity 
351 to distinguish classes of severity during peak season (i.e., September and October) would also be beneficial 
352 to determine competency on efficient drug administration in a resource-limited area. 
353 Equipping healthcare facilities with essential drugs (i.e., prazosin therapy) and educating medical 
354 professionals on management of complicated cases, particularly paediatric victims, by introducing updated 
355 guideline for treatment are essential. Education programs focused on mother-child and adolescent care on 
356 precautionary measures needed to prevent scorpion stings are opportunities to reduce probability of 
357 scorpion sting accidents.  
358 Surveys to determine the typical habitats of scorpions, seasonal variation of scorpion sting prevalence, 
359 and identifying common scorpion species in scorpion sting prevalent regions are important factors to 
360 consider when building effective preventative measures. Since most of the stings are at night, mosquito 
361 nets can protect scorpion stings. In endemic areas of venomous stings, clothing, beddings, shoes, and 
362 packages should be vigorously shaken out and checked for scorpions without blindly putting hands. 
363 Pesticides (i.e., organophosphates, pyrethrums, and chlorinated hydrocarbons) are also known to kill 
364 scorpions.

Abstract 
Background: Limited recent data exist on prescribing patterns and patient 
characteristics for glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), an important 
drug class used as anti-diabetic medication (ADM) for patients with type 2 diabetes 
mellitus (T2D) and/or anti-obesity medication (AOM) in patients with overweight or 
obesity. 
For brevity, we use the term GLP-1 RA to refer to both GLP-1 RA and dual GLP-1 
RA/GIP medications. 
Objective: To describe recent trends in prescribing and dispensing of GLP-1-based 
medications in the US. 
Methods: Using a subset of real-world electronic health record (EHR) data from 
Truveta, a growing collective of health systems that provide more than 18% of all daily 
clinical care in the US, we identified people who were prescribed a GLP-1-based 
medication between January 01, 2018 and June 30, 2024. We describe prescribing 
volumes and patient characteristics over time, by medication, and by FDA-labeled use. 
Among the subset of patients for whom post-prescription dispensing data is available, 
we describe the proportion and characteristics of patients who were and were not 
dispensed a GLP-1 RA following their prescription. 
Results: 1,162,662 patients were prescribed a GLP-1 RA between January 2018 and 
June 2024, with 4,815,135 total prescriptions during this period. Among first-time 
prescriptions for which use could be established, ADMs accounted for 83.0% and 
AOMs accounted for 17.0%. The most common first-time medication was semaglutide 
(n = 644,272). Among those with available data, 70.0% of first-time ADM prescriptions 
overall and 73.7% in March 2024 had a fill within 60 days. By comparison, 43.6% of 
first-time AOM prescriptions overall and 47.2% in March 2024 had a fill within 60 days.

About this report 
This report provides recent trends in the prescribing and dispensing of glucagon-like 
peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RAs)-based medications, including dual GLP-1 
RA/gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP) over time, by medication, and by FDA-labeled 
use. We used near real-time, aggregated electronic health record (EHR) data from a 
collective of US healthcare systems to describe prescribing and dispensing of GLP-1 RA 
medications from January 2018 to June 2024. 
Introduction 
Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) are interconnected epidemics with a high 
prevalence and individual and combined negative impacts on health (CDC, 2020, Hales, 
2020). Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RAs) -based medications, 
including dual GLP-1 RA/gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP), have been shown to 
improve glycemic control in patients with T2D and reduce weight in patients with and 
without T2D (Davies, 2015, Davies, 2021, Garvey, 2023, Jastreboff, 2022, Wilding, 2023, 
Yeh, 2023). GLP-1 RA have also demonstrated cardiovascular benefit in patients with 
and without T2D (Lincoff, 2023, Ussher, 2023). 
Interest in these medications has recently accelerated, largely for their weight-loss 
effects; however, limited empiric data exist on prescribing, dispensing, and patient 
characteristics. Access to and use of GLP-1 RA may be impacted by high cost, limited 
insurance coverage for patients without T2D and medication shortages. 
Methods 
Data 
We evaluated prescribing and dispensing of GLP-1 RAs between January 2018 and June 
2024 using a subset of Truveta Data. Truveta provides access to continuously updated, 
linked, and de-identified electronic health record (EHR) from a collective of US health 
 . CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 International licenseIt is made available under a 
 is the author/funder, who has granted medRxiv a license to display the preprint in perpetuity. (which was not certified by peer review)
The copyright holder for this preprint this version posted July 19, 2024. ; https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.01.18.24301500doi: medRxiv preprint 
care systems that provide 18% of all daily clinical care in the US, including structured 
information on demographics, encounters, diagnoses, vital signs (e.g., weight, BMI, 
blood pressure), medication requests (prescriptions), medication administration, 
laboratory and diagnostic tests and results (e.g., HbA1c tests and values), and 
procedures. Updated EHR data are provided daily to Truveta by member health care 
systems. In addition to EHR data for care delivered within Truveta member health care 
systems, medication dispensing and social drivers of health (SDOH) information are 
made available through linked third-party data. Medication dispense (via e-prescribing 
data) includes fills for prescriptions written both within and outside Truveta member 
health care systems, providing greater observability into patients’ medication history. 
Medication dispense histories are updated at the time of the encounter, and include fill 
dates, NDC or RxNorm codes, quantity dispensed, and days of medication supplied. 
SDOH data include individual-level factors, including income and education. 
Population 
We identified GLP-1 RA prescriptions (medication requests) and dispenses among 
adults using RxNorm and NDC codes for dulaglutide, exenatide, liraglutide, lixisenatide, 
semaglutide, and tirzepatide. Exenatide and lixisenatide were grouped as ‘other’ given 
small relative sizes. Brands were identified when possible using RxNorm and NDC 
codes. Brands labeled for treatment of T2D were classified as ADMs and brands 
labeled for treatment of overweight and obesity were classified as AOMs. When brand 
could not be established, the labeled use was classified as unknown. 
Prescribing Analysis 
Characteristics of patients ever prescribed a GLP-1 RA were summarized, including 
demographics, social drivers of health (SDOH), and presence of T2D and/or overweight 
or obesity. Characteristics are provided by medication and by year of first prescription. 
Overall and first-time prescribing rates of GLP-1 RA were summarized over time by 
medication and labeled use. The prescribing rate was calculated monthly as the 
number of patients with a GLP-1 RA prescription divided by the number of patients 
with any prescription in the month. Absolute differences and percentage changes in 
the rate of GLP-1 RA prescribing over the most recent 3-month period were 
summarized overall and by medication and labeled use. 
Dispensing Analysis 
We describe the proportion of GLP-1 RA prescriptions (overall and first-time) with a 
dispense occurring within 60 days. Dispensing analyses were restricted to 
prescriptions for which complete 60-day dispensing outcomes could be observed.

Dispensing outcomes were considered observable if (1) a dispense was recorded in 
the 60 days following the prescription, and/or (2) an encounter took place after the 60-
day period ended (at which time any dispenses would be observed). To allow sufficient 
follow-up, we report dispensing with a 90-day delay. Given shortages and expected 
substitutions at the pharmacy, we considered the dispense of any GLP-1 RA, which 
could differ from the prescribed GLP-1 RA. 
We plot the proportion of prescriptions (overall and first-time) dispensed within 60 
days over time, by medication and use. Differences in dispensing were expected 
between ADMs and AOMs given ADMs are typically covered by insurance, whereas 
insurance coverage for AOMs is limited. As such, we provide dispensing rates stratified 
by FDA labeled use. Further, we stratify dispensing by age 65+ vs. 18-64 as a proxy for 
Medicare coverage. Medicare never provides coverage for AOMs, whereas commercial 
insurers may.

The paragraph presents Table 4, which describes characteristics of patients aged 65 and older who were prescribed a GLP-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA), stratified by whether they had any GLP-1 RA dispense within 60 days of their first prescription. The real-world problem addressed is understanding medication adherence (dispense status) among older adults initiating GLP-1 RA therapy, a population with high comorbidity burden (e.g., type II diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic kidney disease). The table provides descriptive statistics on demographics (sex, race, ethnicity), clinical characteristics (diabetes, overweight/obesity), specific medications (semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide, dulaglutide), labeled use (ADM vs. AOM), year of prescription, comorbidities, education, and estimated income. These data are intended to characterize the older adult population and identify factors associated with early dispensing versus non-dispensing, which is relevant to optimizing treatment initiation and adherence in this age group.

Discussion and Conclusion 
This analysis summarized GLP-1 RA prescribing trends and patient characteristics from 
January 2018 to June 2024. During this period 1,162,662 patients were prescribed a 
total of 4,815,135 total prescriptions. ADMs accounted for 87.0% of prescriptions, and 
AOMs accounted for 13.0%, among prescriptions where use was known. A larger 
proportion of ADMs, compared to AOMs, were dispensed within 60 days: 70.0% of 
first-time ADM prescriptions and 43.6% of first-time AOM prescriptions had a fill within 
60 days.

Abstract 
During the COVID-19 pandemic it was widely described that certain individuals 
infected by SARS-CoV-2 experience persistent disease signs and symptoms, Long 
COVID, which in some cases is very severe with life changing consequences. To 
maximize our chances of identifying the underpinnings of this illness, we have 
focused on 121 of the most severe cases from >1000 patients screened in specialized 
clinics in Sweden and Belgium. We restricted this study to subjects with objective 
measures of organ damage or dysfunction, >3 months following a verified, but mild-
to-moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection. By performing systems-level immunological 
testing and comparisons to controls fully convalescent following a similar 
mild/moderate COVID-19 episode, we identify elevated serological responses to 
SARS-CoV-2 in severe Long COVID suggestive of chronic antigen stimulation. 
Persistent viral reservoirs have been proposed in Long COVID and using multiple 
orthogonal methods for detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA and protein in plasma we 
identify a subset of patients with detectable antigens, but with minimal overlap 
across assays, and no correlation to symptoms or immune measurements. Elevated 
serologic responses to SARS-CoV-2 on the other hand were inversely correlated with 
clonally expanded memory CD8+ T cells, indicating that restrained clonal expansion 
enables viral persistence, chronic antigen exposure and elevated IgG responses, even 
if antigen-detection in blood is not universally possible.
final_conclusion: The article addresses the real-world problem of severe Long COVID, specifically persistent disease signs and symptoms following mild-to-moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection that cause life-changing consequences. It focuses on identifying the underpinnings of this illness by studying the most severe cases with objective organ damage or dysfunction. The study finds elevated serological responses to SARS-CoV-2 suggesting chronic antigen stimulation, and proposes that restrained clonal expansion of memory CD8+ T cells enables viral persistence, chronic antigen exposure, and elevated IgG responses, even though antigen detection in blood is not universally possible.

Introduction 
Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infections cause a 
wide range of disease manifestations from asymptomatic or mild infection, 
predominantly in the young1, to deadly COVID-19 pneumonia associated with 
hyperinflammation and coagulopathy leading to multiorgan failure and death2. The 
main determinant of developing life-threatening COVID-19 pneumonia is whether a 
timely type-I Interferon (IFN-I) response is elicited by infected respiratory epithelial 
cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDC), which then limits viral replication and 
allows for T cells and antibodies to clear the virus. This is illustrated by life-
threatening COVID-19 in individuals with inborn errors of the IFN-I activity3, or 
individuals carrying neutralizing autoantibodies to IFN-I4.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of understanding why SARS-CoV-2 infections range from asymptomatic/mild to deadly COVID-19 pneumonia. Specifically, it identifies the failure to elicit a timely type-I interferon (IFN-I) response by infected respiratory epithelial cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells as the main determinant of life-threatening COVID-19 pneumonia, supported by evidence from individuals with inborn errors of IFN-I activity or neutralizing autoantibodies to IFN-I.

original_paragraph:
We have also learned that certain children develop a post-infectious condition 
following mild SARS-CoV-2 infection with severe hyperinflammation, skin rashes, 
abdominal pain and sometimes overt intestinal inflammation5. This Multisystem 
Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) overlaps in part with the postinfectious 
vasculitis syndrome, Kawasaki disease, but immunological perturbations distinguish 
these conditions6. Intriguingly, the development of MIS-C has been linked to viral 
persistence in the gut7, and perhaps repeated activation of T cells via a pathway 
reminiscent of superantigen-mediated T cell activation8–11. Prior to this observation, 
Cheng and colleagues reported a possible superantigen-motif within the SARS-CoV-
2 spike protein that exhibited similarity to staphylococcal enterotoxin B12, but more

recently, similar T cell skewing has also been shown in pre-pandemic samples, 
indicating that other pathogens, like seasonal coronaviruses, could trigger similar 
reactions13. Moreover, recessive defects of the OAS-RNAse L pathway have been 
shown to explain some cases of MIS-C, indicating that heightened inflammatory 
responses by monocytes and other mononuclear phagocytes contribute to MIS-C14. 
Genetic factors predisposing to post-infectious Long COVID are under investigation 
and have not been described yet. Nevertheless, it is tempting to speculate that both 
postinfectious MIS-C and Long COVID could involve shared mechanisms. We have 
proposed disease tolerance, restrained antiviral T cell responses and viral persistence 
as one such possible mechanism15. In growing children, efficient antiviral responses 
in the airways16, could allow for prioritization of limited resources towards stature 
growth over systemic inflammatory responses leading to mild COVID-19, but 
potentially also enable viral persistence and MIS-C15. In women of reproductive age, 
efficient antiviral responses limit viral replication better than in males and could allow 
similar prioritization of limited resources for investments into reproduction, over 
antiviral T cell responses and systemic inflammation, leading to mild COVID-19 in 
most, but also an increased likelihood for viral persistence and higher incidence of 
Long COVID15. Viral persistence has been proposed to be the key unifying feature 
among these postinfectious conditions, as suggested by multiple reports involving 
plasma samples17–19, tissue imaging20, and tissue specimens from patients21,22, as well 
as indirect evidence of continued somatic hypermutation in SARS-CoV-2 specific B 
cells, months after initial infection23.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of post-infectious conditions following mild SARS-CoV-2 infection, specifically Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) and Long COVID. It discusses the clinical features of MIS-C (severe hyperinflammation, skin rashes, abdominal pain, intestinal inflammation), its overlap and distinction from Kawasaki disease, and proposed mechanisms including viral persistence in the gut, superantigen-like T cell activation, genetic defects in the OAS-RNAse L pathway, and disease tolerance. The paragraph concludes by hypothesizing that viral persistence is a key unifying feature among these post-infectious conditions, potentially explaining shared mechanisms between MIS-C and Long COVID, with age- and sex-specific differences in antiviral responses and resource prioritization (growth in children, reproduction in women) contributing to mild acute COVID-19 but increased risk of viral persistence and post-infectious sequelae.

original_paragraph:
Long COVID or post-acute COVID-19 syndrome represents a wide spectrum of 
diverse symptoms ranging from mild cognitive impairment and fatigue to 
debilitating autonomic dysregulation, microvascular dysfunction, and sometimes life-
threatening tissue damage24. It is well established that vaccines reduce the risk but 
do not fully prevent the development of Long COVID25, and early therapy with 
antiviral medication following SARS-CoV-2 infection also reduces the risk of 
developing Long COVID26. These observations offer further support to the hypothesis 
that viral persistence is a possible cause of postinfectious Long COVID. We have 
formed a Long COVID subgroup within the international COVID-Human Genetic 
Effort Consortium (https://www.covidhge.com/), a group investigating diverse 
disease manifestations following SARS-CoV-2 infections by sharing and aggregating 
data from around the world27. We focus on severe cases with objective measures of 
organ dysfunction and damage following mild to moderate SARS-CoV-2 infections28.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of Long COVID (post-acute COVID-19 syndrome), a condition with diverse symptoms ranging from mild cognitive impairment and fatigue to debilitating autonomic dysregulation, microvascular dysfunction, and potentially life-threatening tissue damage. It notes that vaccines and early antiviral therapy reduce but do not fully prevent Long COVID, supporting the hypothesis that viral persistence may cause postinfectious Long COVID. The authors formed a Long COVID subgroup within the international COVID-Human Genetic Effort Consortium to investigate severe cases with objective measures of organ dysfunction and damage following mild to moderate SARS-CoV-2 infections.

Here we report that patients with severe Long COVID present with variable 
symptoms, do not cluster in relation to organs affected or immunological states. 
Serologic responses to SARS-CoV-2 are strongly elevated in severe Long COVID 
patients as compared to convalescent controls indicating persistent antigen 
stimulation. Direct analyses of SARS-CoV-2 RNA and protein antigens in plasma 
using multiple orthogonal methods reveal subsets of antigen positive individuals, but

uniformly detectable in plasma and that elevated serological responses is a more

final_conclusion: The article addresses the real-world problem of severe Long COVID by investigating its variable symptoms, lack of clustering by organ or immunological state, and the underlying mechanisms. It finds that elevated serological responses to SARS-CoV-2 indicate persistent antigen stimulation, while direct detection of viral RNA/protein in plasma is inconsistent across assays, suggesting viral persistence is not uniformly detectable and that serology is a more sensitive marker. It also identifies innate immune markers correlating with elevated IgG and persistent inflammation, and an inverse correlation between clonally expanded SARS-CoV-2-specific memory CD8+ T cells and IgG responses, supporting the hypothesis of viral persistence with restrained cytotoxic CD8+ T cell responses as a possible mechanism in severe Long COVID.

Results 
Identifying patients with severe Long COVID and objective measures of disease. 
The diagnosis of Long COVID is vaguely defined and to ensure that all patients 
enrolled have an organic cause of persistent symptoms, we screened >1,000 subjects 
at Long COVID clinics in Leuven, Belgium & Karolinska University Hospital in 
Stockholm, Sweden to find the most severe cases (Fig. 1a). Among these subjects, 
we only included subjects with a verified history of SARS-CoV-2 infection and mild to 
moderate COVID-19 course (non-hospitalized patients) to avoid overlap with the 
related post-intensive care syndrome which is also associated with prolonged 
cognitive and physiological symptoms partially overlapping with those reported in 
Long COVID29. We also limited our inclusion to subjects with objective measures of 
disease and organ damage which included microvascular dysfunction shown by 
magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the heart, endothelial dysfunction by pulsatile 
arterial tonometry (EndoPAT), autonomic dysfunction and postural orthostatic 
tachycardia syndrome (POTS), hyperventilation, pulmonary air trapping or reduced 
carbon monoxide diffusion capacity and other respiratory abnormalities which can be 
objectively measured by computer tomography (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Fig. 
1a). We included 121 patients in Belgium (n=31) and Sweden (n=90), of which 87% 
were female and average age was 48 (min-max, 14-72 years). Numbers of symptoms 
were variable in each subject and did not follow any obvious grouping within the 
cohort (Fig. 1b).
final_conclusion: The article addresses the real-world problem of the vague and poorly defined diagnosis of Long COVID, which complicates the identification of patients with genuine organic causes of persistent symptoms. To overcome this, the authors screened over 1,000 subjects at Long COVID clinics in Belgium and Sweden to isolate the most severe cases, restricting inclusion to non-hospitalized patients with verified SARS-CoV-2 infection and mild-to-moderate COVID-19 to avoid overlap with post-intensive care syndrome. They further required objective measures of disease and organ damage—including microvascular dysfunction on cardiac MRI, endothelial dysfunction by EndoPAT, autonomic dysfunction/POTS, hyperventilation, pulmonary air trapping, reduced carbon monoxide diffusion capacity, and other respiratory abnormalities on CT—ultimately enrolling 121 patients (87% female, average age 48). Thus, the study addresses the need for a more precise, objective characterization of severe Long COVID to support reliable diagnosis and research.

Elevated serological responses to SARS-CoV-2 in severe Long COVID. 
We measured antibody responses against SARS-CoV-2 using in-house ELISA assays 
and found that IgG responses were elevated compared to convalescent controls30 in 
both Belgian and Swedish Long COVID patients (Fig. 1c), however, no clear 
differences were observed for plasma IgA or IgM responses to SARS-CoV-2 viruses 
(Fig. 1d-e). Since standard ELISA assays are not as sensitive as single-molecule array 
(SIMOA) assays31, also for detecting SARS-CoV-2 specific IgGs32, we performed 
SIMOA assays and compared absolute IgG antibody concentrations (pg/ml) in 
relation to the time from first known SARS-CoV-2 infection (Fig. 1f). Results showed 
an even more pronounced difference between patients with severe Long COVID and 
convalescent controls, a finding that was especially clear in the Swedish cohort which

striking considering that these Long COVID cases were sampled long after their acute

final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of understanding the immunological characteristics of Long COVID, specifically whether severe Long COVID is associated with elevated serological (antibody) responses to SARS-CoV-2. Using ELISA and SIMOA assays, the authors found that IgG responses were elevated in Long COVID patients compared to convalescent controls—especially in severe cases and in the Swedish cohort—while no clear differences were observed for plasma IgA or IgM. The elevated IgG persisted long after acute infection despite the expected decline over time, and this pattern could not be explained by vaccination timing or rates. Thus, the paragraph concludes that severe Long COVID is associated with pronounced and sustained elevations in SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG responses.

Persistent antigens are found in a subset of patients but with little overlap between 
assays used.

persistent antigens and even viral reservoirs21. We therefore searched for persistent 
SARS-CoV-2 antigens in plasma samples using the SIMOA assay following reduction 
of endogenous SARS-CoV-2 antibodies as previously described18. Total spike protein 
was detectable in 10/100 Long COVID patients and 2/50 convalescent controls (Fig.

2a). The S1 subunit of spike was detectable in fewer patients as previously observed 
in two other cohorts18,19 (Fig. 2b), while the N antigen was detectable in 10/100 Long 
COVID cases, but only 1/50 convalescent controls (Fig. 2c). This latter finding is 
significant as it cannot be explained by vaccinations where the N protein is not

a subset of ~10% of patients with severe Long COVID.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of identifying persistent SARS-CoV-2 antigens in patients with Long COVID. Using the SIMOA assay after reducing endogenous antibodies, the study found that total spike protein was detectable in 10/100 Long COVID patients versus 2/50 convalescent controls, the S1 subunit in fewer patients, and the N antigen in 10/100 Long COVID cases versus only 1/50 controls. The N antigen finding is significant because it cannot be explained by vaccination (which does not include N protein). The conclusion is that persistent SARS-CoV-2 antigens are detectable in a subset of approximately 10% of patients with severe Long COVID, supporting the hypothesis that persistent antigens and viral reservoirs may contribute to elevated serological responses in Long COVID.

To further investigate the detection of persistent spike protein in these same plasma 
samples, we also tested an orthogonal assay for S1 subunit of spike, the SPEAR 
immunoassay™ (SpearBio, Boston, MA). We found many more positive signals 
among both Long COVID (20/100) and convalescent control subjects (13/50), with no 
difference between these two groups (Fig. 2d). Both the two Long COVID patients 
with detectable S1 spike by SIMOA were also positive using the SPEAR immunoassay 
with a threshold of 16 as level of detection, while the one convalescent control 
CP164b was not (Fig. 2d). We also analyzed SARS-CoV-2 RNA using an nCounter 
(Nanostring technologies)34 in 28 of the Long COVID subjects from Belgium. Using 
antisense RNA from SARS-CoV-2 as a marker of ongoing viral replication we 
identified one subject (MGA033) positive for both antisense RNA and plasma spike

final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of whether persistent SARS-CoV-2 viral antigens or ongoing viral replication can be reliably detected in the plasma of Long COVID patients compared with convalescent controls. Using orthogonal assays (SIMOA, SPEAR immunoassay, and nCounter RNA analysis), the authors found that antigen positivity was common in both groups, with only slight enrichment in Long COVID patients; two or more detectable antigens occurred only in Long COVID patients (~10% of the cohort), and no clear link was observed between plasma antigen levels and symptom groups. The authors conclude that the assays may lack sufficient sensitivity to detect all plasma antigens, that tissue-confined viral reservoirs may not leak antigens into plasma, or that viral persistence is not a universal feature of Long COVID—though this last possibility conflicts with persistently elevated SARS-CoV-2 IgG responses seen in Long COVID cohorts.

original_paragraph:
Innate responses in Long COVID patients with elevated serological responses  
to SARS-CoV-2. 
Given that persistent antigen in plasma was not universal to all Long COVID cases, 
while elevated IgG responses to SARS-CoV-2 (SIMOA assay) more clearly 
distinguished patients from convalescent controls, we reasoned that elevated IgG 
responses might be a more sensitive biomarker to pursue further in patients with 
Long COVID. To understand possible immunological correlates associated with 
elevated SARS-CoV-2 IgG responses and possibly persistent virus, we assessed ~26.5 
million whole blood immune cells by mass cytometry using a 51-parameter panel. 
After clustering these cells using self-organizing maps38, we manually annotated the 
116 clusters based on known marker combinations (Supplementary Fig. 1b). The 
cluster abundances were assessed against SARS-CoV-2 specific IgG responses 
measured by SIMOA as a proxy for antigen persistence. Three clusters of classical 
monocytes were inversely correlated with SARS-CoV-2 specific IgG (#71, #91 and 
#92), and one monocyte cluster (#81) expressing high CD33 was positively correlated 
with elevated anti-spike IgG responses (Fig. 3a-b). CD33-expressing classical 
monocytes have previously been associated with anti-tumor immune responses and 
favourable responses to checkpoint inhibition in lung cancer39, and its blockade 
triggers spontaneous production of TNFa, IL-1b and IL-8 suggesting a repressive 
function in monocytes40. Expansion of CD33-expressing monocytes over CD33-
negative monocytes in patients with Long COVID and elevated antibody responses 
(Fig. 3a-b), indicates an attempt at dampening a persistent innate immune response 
to persistent antigen. To investigate the levels of cytokines and other plasma 
proteins we carried out Olink assays (Target inflammation™, Olink, Uppsala, Sweden) 
and correlated protein levels (normalized protein expression, NPX) to SARS-CoV-2 
specific IgG levels. The most highly correlated proteins were circulating CD40, PD-L1, 
TRAIL and TNFa supporting an ongoing immune response in these patients, but not 
in convalescent control subjects (Fig. 3c). We conclude from these findings that 
patients with Long COVID display evidence of an ongoing innate response involving 
monocyte subsets and plasma proteins involved in antiviral and inflammatory 
responses.
final_conclusion: The article addresses the real-world problem of identifying immunological correlates and potential biomarkers in Long COVID patients with elevated SARS-CoV-2 IgG responses. It concludes that these patients display evidence of an ongoing innate immune response involving specific monocyte subsets (e.g., CD33-expressing classical monocytes) and plasma proteins (CD40, PD-L1, TRAIL, TNFa) related to antiviral and inflammatory responses, suggesting persistent antigen-driven immune activation.

Lack of autoantibodies targeting IFN-I in patients with severe Long COVID 
Autoantibodies to type-I IFN have been associated with life-threatening COVID-19 
pneumonia4 due to impaired IFN-I-mediated inhibition of viral replication. Such 
autoantibodies increase in frequency with age, are more common in males than 
females for unknown reason and could explain up to 20% COVID-19 deaths41. The 
reasons for the development of anti-cytokine autoantibodies are unknown in most 
cases, but most if not all patients with inborn errors of central tolerance due to AIRE 
deficiency in cis (APECED or APS1) or in trans (mutations of the alternative NF-kB

pathway) all carry these autoantibodies and are highly susceptible to severe SARS-
CoV-2 infections42–44. Since the patients with Long COVID in our cohort generally had 
mild to moderate acute COVID-19, we reasoned that autoantibodies to IFN-I were 
unlikely to be involved at the time of initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, but that de novo 
production of such autoantibodies following the SARS-CoV-2 infection could cause 
viral resurgence, persistence and Long COVID. We investigated levels of 
autoantibodies to four different IFNa subtypes and IL1RN but found no evidence of 
these autoantibodies in patients with Long COVID (Supplementary Fig. 2).
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of whether autoantibodies targeting type-I interferons (IFN-I) contribute to the development of severe Long COVID. The authors hypothesized that de novo production of anti-IFN-I autoantibodies after SARS-CoV-2 infection could cause viral resurgence, persistence, and Long COVID. However, they found no evidence of autoantibodies to four IFNα subtypes or IL1RN in patients with Long COVID, concluding that such autoantibodies are unlikely to be involved in Long COVID in their cohort.

original_paragraph:
Lack of evidence for superantigen-mediated T cell responses in Long COVID patients. 
If persistent antigen, and possibly replicating viral particles are responsible for 
elevated anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike IgG levels and elevated markers of inflammation in 
patients with Long COVID, questions regarding the quality of the T cell response 
arise. We therefore performed single-cell TCR and mRNA-sequencing in peripheral 
blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from n=30 subjects with severe Long COVID and 
n=12 convalescent controls. In the postinfectious disorder MIS-C in children 
following SARS-CoV-2 infection, a skewing of T cell repertoires has been widely 
reported8,11,45,46. This involves the selective expansion of T cells carrying Vb21 
(TRBV11-2) paired with variable Va genes, suggestive of a possible superantigen-
mediated T cell activation and expansion. Here we find no evidence for such 
expansion events, either among Long COVID or convalescent controls, in either 
memory CD8+ T cells (Fig. 4a), or memory CD4+ T cells (Fig. 4b). This further 
suggests that MIS-C and Long COVID operate via distinct mechanisms.
final_conclusion: The article addresses the real-world problem of understanding the immunological mechanisms underlying Long COVID, specifically testing whether superantigen-mediated T cell responses (as seen in MIS-C) contribute to the condition. The analysis found no evidence of such T cell repertoire skewing or expansion in Long COVID patients or convalescent controls, indicating that Long COVID and MIS-C operate via distinct mechanisms.

original_paragraph:
SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses. 
To investigate the specificity of T cell responses is challenging with the gold standard 
method being multimer-tagging of antigen-specific T cells or restimulation assays. 
An alternative method is to infer antigen-specificity from TCR sequences, an area 
where important advances have been made in recent years. One such advancement 
is the clustering of T cell receptor Va and Vb sequences based on similarities in the 
specific amino acid residues of the Complementary Determining Region (CDR) 3 with 
greatest impact on peptide/MHC complex specificity47. Here we used this GLIPH 
method in its most updated version48 and clustered memory CD8 T cell TCR 
sequences (Fig. 4c). Based on prior data from multimer-sorted T cells with known 
specificities for Influenza A and B viruses, Cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus 
(EBV) and SARS-CoV-2 respectively49,50, new TCR sequence clusters obtained from 
Long COVID patients and convalescent controls could be mapped to these known 
specificities (Fig. 4c).
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the challenge of investigating the specificity of SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses, since the gold standard methods (multimer-tagging of antigen-specific T cells or restimulation assays) are difficult. It proposes inferring antigen-specificity from TCR sequences using the updated GLIPH clustering method, and shows that new TCR sequence clusters from Long COVID patients and convalescent controls can be mapped to known specificities for Influenza A/B, CMV, EBV, and SARS-CoV-2 based on prior multimer-sorted data.

Association between SARS-CoV-2 specific T cell responses and antibody responses. 
The fraction of T cell clusters identified through GLIPH2 which mapped to likely 
SARS-CoV-2 specificity was 604 in Long COVID and 232 in convalescent controls. 
This expansion of T cells specific for SARS-CoV-2 in Long COVID is in line with

between overall clonal expansion of memory CD8+ T cells and anti-spike IgG levels 
(Fig. 4d). However, when focusing on the fraction of memory CD8+ T cells mapping 
to SARS-CoV-2 by GLIPH2, an inverse relationship was found between the expansion 
of such cells and plasma anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike IgG levels (Fig. 4e). This result 
suggests that individuals who fail to mount a clonally expanded memory CD8+ T cell 
response to SARS-CoV-2 develop a viral reservoir with persistent antigen that drive 
up an elevated anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike IgG response with time. This contrast with the 
normal tapering of IgG titers over time following infections in convalescent 
individuals23,51.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of understanding the immune mechanisms underlying Long COVID, specifically the relationship between SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell responses and antibody responses. It finds that Long COVID patients show greater expansion of SARS-CoV-2-specific T cell clusters (604 vs. 232 in convalescent controls), consistent with elevated IgG responses and antigen persistence. While overall memory CD8+ T cell clonal expansion is not linked to anti-spike IgG levels, the fraction of memory CD8+ T cells mapping to SARS-CoV-2 is inversely related to plasma anti-spike IgG levels. This suggests that individuals who fail to mount a clonally expanded memory CD8+ T cell response may develop a viral reservoir with persistent antigen, driving elevated anti-spike IgG over time—contrasting with the normal IgG tapering seen in convalescent individuals. Thus, the paragraph highlights the problem of persistent antigen and dysregulated immune responses in Long COVID.

original_paragraph:
We further characterized this memory CD8+ T cell response by comparing mRNA 
transcript levels between patients with high and low anti-SARS-CoV-2 spike IgG 
levels respectively. We found that individuals with lower levels of anti-spike IgG 
displayed a memory CD8+ T cell response with upregulation of molecules associated 
with cytotoxic Th1 responses such as GZMB, GZMH, IFNG, TNF and NKG7 (Fig. 4f). 
Patients with higher anti-spike IgG levels and possible viral persistence had a higher 
expression of KIR3DL1 (Fig. 4f), an NK cell receptor recently shown to be a marker of 
regulatory CD8+ T cells52. The function of these cells is to kill CD4+ T cells and limit 
autoimmune responses following infections, and accordingly, they have been found 
to be expanded in patients with SARS-CoV-2 infections52.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of understanding the heterogeneity of memory CD8+ T cell responses in SARS-CoV-2 infection in relation to anti-spike IgG levels. It finds that individuals with lower anti-spike IgG have a cytotoxic Th1-like memory CD8+ T cell profile (upregulation of GZMB, GZMH, IFNG, TNF, NKG7), whereas those with higher anti-spike IgG and possible viral persistence show increased KIR3DL1 expression, a marker of regulatory CD8+ T cells that kill CD4+ T cells and limit autoimmune responses and are expanded in SARS-CoV-2 infection.

original_paragraph:
Moreover, a recent immunomonitoring study reported evidence of T cell exhaustion 
in patients with Long COVID, to a greater extent than in convalescent controls, 
without taking the antigen specificity of such cells into account37. We therefore 
investigated mRNA transcripts in individual memory CD8+ T cells from Long COVID 
patients with high and low levels of SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG responses respectively, 
but no significant differences between these subgroups were observed (Fig. 4g). This 
indicates that T cell exhaustion does not explain failure to expand productive 
memory CD8+ T cell responses to clear viral reservoirs in patients with Long COVID.
final_conclusion: The real-world problem addressed is understanding why patients with Long COVID fail to clear viral reservoirs despite having SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG responses. The study investigates whether T cell exhaustion explains this failure by examining mRNA transcripts in individual memory CD8+ T cells from Long COVID patients with high versus low levels of SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG. No significant differences were found between these subgroups, indicating that T cell exhaustion does not explain the failure to expand productive memory CD8+ T cell responses to clear viral reservoirs in Long COVID patients.

original_paragraph:
Long COVID is a heterogeneous condition lacking clear diagnostic tests or even solid 
criteria, leading to a great deal of debate surrounding the condition and further 
complicating the interpretation of data regarding incidence and severity in 
populations infected by SARS-CoV-2. Here we have focused on the 121 most severe 
patients we have been able to identify out of >1000 cases screened in specialized 
Long COVID clinics in Stockholm and Leuven, all with objective measures of organ 
damage or dysfunction following mild to moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection2. By doing 
so, we maximize our chances of identifying the underlying biological perturbation in 
Long COVID and we have uncovered several immunological perturbations in these 
cases as compared to convalescent controls fully recovered following SARS-CoV-2 
infections.
final_conclusion: The article addresses the real-world problem of Long COVID being a heterogeneous condition without clear diagnostic tests or solid criteria, which creates debate and complicates interpretation of incidence and severity data. To overcome this, the authors focus on the 121 most severe patients out of >1000 screened in specialized clinics, all with objective organ damage or dysfunction after mild to moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection, thereby maximizing the chance of identifying underlying biological perturbations and uncovering immunological perturbations compared with fully recovered convalescent controls.

original_paragraph:
Numerous previous studies have reported the presence of SARS-CoV-2 viral particles 
or SARS-CoV-2 protein antigens, long after an initial infection21. Direct 
measurements of circulating SARS-CoV-2 spike proteins in the plasma of patients 
with Long COVID have also been reported18,19.  Imaging studies have suggested 
persistent T cell activation and viral reservoirs in Long COVID20, and tissue biopsy 
studies have reported persistent viral proteins21 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, 
but these are not always associated with persistent symptoms23. Antibody titers 
normally wane in plasma within 6 months of initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, but 
memory B cells can show continued somatic hypermutation suggesting viral 
persistence for months, even in individuals without Long COVID23. One study 
reported inverse correlation between anti-N IgG responses in the first ten days 
following primary SARS-CoV-2 infection and the risk of developing Long COVID53 
and this might seem at odds with the elevated IgG responses reported herein and by 
others37,54 in patients with Long COVID cases, but this likely reflects differences 
between the initial and the long-term adaptive responses to SARS-CoV-2. A strong 
initial adaptive response might increase the chance of viral clearance and reduce the 
risk of Long COVID, while a sustained and elevated long-term response to SARS-
CoV-2 with elevated titers occur once a viral reservoir has been established leading 
to chronic antigen stimulation.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of understanding the biological mechanisms underlying Long COVID, specifically whether SARS-CoV-2 viral particles, proteins, or reservoirs persist after initial infection and how these relate to persistent symptoms. It synthesizes evidence of viral persistence and chronic antigen stimulation, and reconciles seemingly contradictory findings about antibody responses—strong early responses may aid viral clearance and reduce Long COVID risk, while elevated long-term antibody titers may reflect an established viral reservoir driving chronic stimulation. The core problem is elucidating the relationship between viral persistence, immune response dynamics, and the development and maintenance of Long COVID symptoms.

original_paragraph:
Reports of innate cell perturbations in patients with Long COVID have been 
published but results are variable and somewhat conflicting55. We find monocyte 
redistribution in favor of CD33-expressing classical monocytes in Long COVID and 
elevated plasma proteins such as TNFa and TRAIL suggesting ongoing monocyte 
activation, in line with previous findings56,57. Another recent paper reported a

antibody-responses, either to SARS-CoV-2 or to reactivated herpesviruses58. 
Reactivation of chronic viruses has also been discussed as an initial determinant of 
Long COVID in patients with acute COVID-19, EBV reactivation signified patients 
more likely to develop persistent symptoms59. Accordingly, elevated levels of anti-
EBV antibodies were reported in one recent study of Long COVID as compared to 
convalescent controls37. We assessed levels of IgG against EA, VCA, EBNA1 or gp42 
of EBV, as well as IgM targeting gp42 and VCA but found no significant differences 
between Long COVID patients and convalescent controls (Supplementary Fig. 3). 
We conclude that the role of chronic viral reactivation as an underlying explanation 
for Long COVID remains unclear but could contribute to complement activation and 
microclots seen in some patients60.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of understanding the underlying mechanisms of Long COVID, specifically whether innate immune cell perturbations (monocyte redistribution and activation), complement system dysregulation, and chronic viral reactivation (particularly EBV) contribute to the condition. The authors found evidence of monocyte redistribution and activation but no significant differences in anti-EBV antibody levels between Long COVID patients and convalescent controls, concluding that the role of chronic viral reactivation remains unclear but could contribute to complement activation and microclots in some patients.

original_paragraph:
Our finding that SARS-CoV-2 specific CD8+ T cells were less expanded in Long COVID 
cases at a frequency that was inversely correlated with the elevated serologic 
response, suggests a restrained antiviral T cell response as a key aspect of Long 
COVID pathology. Others have suggested an exhausted T cell responses in Long 
COVID based on elevated PD-1 expression and other marker changes37,61 but in our 
analyses we find no difference in exhaustion markers in relation to IgG responses, 
suggesting that the failure in viral clearance arises earlier as a consequence of a 
restrained antiviral CD8+ T cell response permitting the establishment of a viral 
reservoir and the development of Long COVID. It is interesting to speculate about 
the reasons for why predominantly females of reproductive age and children are at 
risk of developing postinfectious disorders (MIS-C and Long COVID) associated with 
SARS-CoV-2 persistence. One already known common feature of children and 
women of reproductive age is the very efficient IFN-I responses during acute SARS 
CoV-2 infection15. In mice the timing and source of IFN-I can either suppress or 
potentiate an antiviral CD8+ T cell response62 and one possible mechanisms thereof 
is balanced IFN-I mediated activation of STAT1 over STAT4 where the former is 
restraining CD8+ T cell responses and the latter potentiates them following viral 
infections63. Ongoing work in our laboratories are looking for possible genetic causes 
underlying the failure to clear SARS-Cov2 viruses and development of Long COVID27. 
All in all, our results suggest that a persistent viral reservoir is likely contributing to 
Long COVID pathology and ongoing efforts (NCT05823896) to remove such 
persisting viruses with prolonged antiviral therapies are important and hold clinical 
promise for delivering a much-needed cure to the community of Long COVID 
sufferers worldwide.
final_conclusion: The paragraph addresses the real-world problem of Long COVID pathology, specifically the failure to clear SARS-CoV-2 and the development of a persistent viral reservoir. It identifies a restrained antiviral CD8+ T cell response—less expanded in Long COVID cases and inversely correlated with elevated serologic response—as a key mechanism, rather than T cell exhaustion, suggesting the failure in viral clearance arises earlier. It also considers why predominantly females of reproductive age and children are at risk of postinfectious disorders (MIS-C and Long COVID), linking this to efficient IFN-I responses and possible IFN-I-mediated STAT1/STAT4 balance restraining CD8+ T cell responses. The authors conclude that a persistent viral reservoir likely contributes to Long COVID pathology and that ongoing clinical efforts (NCT05823896) using prolonged antiviral therapies to remove persisting viruses hold promise for a cure for Long COVID sufferers worldwide.

Vestibular agnosia is linked to worse balance recovery in traumatic brain injury: a 
longitudinal behavioural and neuro-imaging study
final_conclusion: The article addresses the real-world problem of poor balance recovery following traumatic brain injury (TBI). Specifically, it investigates whether vestibular agnosia—a deficit in perceiving vestibular signals—is associated with worse balance outcomes in TBI patients, using longitudinal behavioral assessments and neuroimaging to understand this relationship.
